items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Aker had a private membership club in Soho on Greek Street, which was directed by his brother Dave and I spent quite a few after hours there with Lily, members of Aker's orchestra and jazz fans.

ctx.x: In October I recorded with Alix Combelle whom I spoke of before as being one of the first French jazz musicians that I became acquainted in 1935. The pianist was a New Yorker named David Martin who's family had a music school on 136th Street between 7th Avenue and Lenox. Dave

accompanied quite a few classical musicians and singers and was in Europe at this time accompanying Eddie South who was known as the "Dark Angel of the violin". Dave was also known as a jazz pianist and that was the reason he was on this date which was recorded under the name of Combelle. Wilson Meyers was on bass, Roger Chaput guitar and Jerry Mengo drums. We recorded four numbers of which "Hang Over Blues" was my composition.

"Hang Over Blues" was just a name that I decided on and not because I had a hangover. Another number was recorded but never issued. It was "Sometimes I'm Happy". I never found out why it was never issued and have no idea what it really sounded like. This Combelle record was recorded the 4th of October 1937.
